03How It Fits TogetherSYSTEM▶

The client tracking system is one orchestrator skill plus one module skill per channel. You talk to client-desk; it sets up each client and calls the modules that client uses. The page builders live in a separate private repo, the build kit, so every client gets the same pages. Every name follows one format, so a client's Claude project, Drive folder, Fusion project and repo always match.

  • Account-wideSkills are saved once to your account and work in every Claude project; nothing is copied per project.
  • One project eachEach client gets its own Claude project, so memory, threads and files never mix.
  • Skill buildingSkills are drafted and fixed in the "Client Desk (skill building)" project, never in a client's project.
  • On requestUpdates run only when you ask ("update all", "Messenger update since last"). Nothing is scheduled.
  • Private firstEvery page starts private, and the NDA check runs before every publish.

The same system as a tree: open a branch to see what sits inside it.

04Skills and ModulesSKILLS▶

Two skills are live and saved to your account. Five modules are planned and get built the first time a client needs each one (Stage 4 of the plan). A planned module is never improvised: client-desk says it is missing and offers to build it in the skill-building project.

05Client LifecycleLIFECYCLE▶

A client moves between three statuses: Active, Paused and Closed. Every change is written to project.json as a dated status_log entry with your reason, and the hub shows the status as a badge. Nothing is ever renamed or moved, so every link anyone has keeps working.

TopicStatus afterYou sayWhat Claude does
SetupSetup"set up client <name>"Writes project.json with status Active and the first status_log entry (reason "Started")
ActiveActivedefault after setupUpdates run whenever you ask
PausedPaused"pause client"Logs date and reason; hub badge and tracker rebuilt; "update all" skips the client
ClosedClosed"close client"Logs date and reason; pages, folders and repo stay exactly where they are
ReopenActive again"reopen client"Logs it, rebuilds the pages, then runs "since last" on every channel from where it stopped
Example log{"date": "2026-12-03", "status": "Paused", "reason": "Waiting on prototype"} then {"date": "2027-01-10", "status": "Active", "reason": "Reopened"}. The catch-up finds nothing lost and nothing duplicated, because each channel keeps its own "since last" mark in state/channels.json.
06Setup and Daily UseLIFECYCLE▶

Setting up a client takes about 10 to 20 minutes of your time, mostly answering the intake questions. Claude posts a checklist and keeps working while it waits.

  1. ClientFull name, exact spelling, and what to call them.
  2. HistoryNew or previous client; if previous, roughly when the work started.
  3. TitleTitle and Details (exact spelling, CamelCase), and whether there is a product to launch.
  4. SourceFB (default), Email, Referral, Web, InPerson or Other.
  5. ChannelsMessenger (with the chat link), email, Zoom (with or without Fathom), Drive, phone or in person.
  6. EmailThe client's email, if known.
  7. Time zoneDefault Eastern.
  8. SharingEverything private (default), or share now.
  9. NDAAny NDA or privacy limits.
  • New messagesSay "Messenger update since last": a new chat page, images filed in Drive, tracker and hub updated.
  • EverythingSay "update all" to run every live module for every active client, then rebuild hub and tracker once.
  • Check inSay "client status" for a short summary with links.
  • Previous clientThe first update is a backfill of the whole history.

Every name for a client is built from the intake answers and shown to you once, before anything is created. The repo name always waits for your OK.

Project name to repo nameSplit each CamelCase word at its capitals and keep runs of capitals together, join words with hyphens and groups with underscores, then lower-case it: TestWidget(DemoPart)(JaneDoe,FB) → test-widget + demo-part + jane-doe + fb → test-widget_demo-part_jane-doe_fb.
  • SpellingClient and product spellings are stored at intake and used everywhere, exactly.
  • No spacesNo spaces anywhere in the project name; each word starts with a capital.
  • Repo firstClaude can't create a GitHub repo: it gives you the exact name and a one-click link, and keeps working meanwhile.
  • RenamesRenames are done by you in GitHub or Drive settings, and only when you ask.

09Drive for Desktop WorkflowDRIVE▶

There is no separate local folder. The client folder lives in Drive, and Google Drive for desktop keeps it on your computer, with Projects set to Mirror or Available offline. Fusion documents stay in Autodesk's cloud; the skills record design names and versions and save exports to Drive.

  1. InstallInstall Google Drive for desktop and sign in with the account that owns Projects.
  2. OfflineChoose Mirror files, or right-click Projects and pick Available offline, so client files open without a connection.
  3. WorkOpen and save client files straight in Projects/<project name>; they sync on their own.
  4. FusionKeep Fusion designs in the Fusion project of the same name; save exports into 04 Design/v##.
Upload lessonClaude copies each file into its own working folder first, checks it, uploads it to Drive, then logs the Drive link in the tracker. Uploading from the shared project folder can change image bytes.

14GlossarySource▶

Every term with a dotted underline in the dashboard links here — hover it for a quick definition, click it to land on its row. In the Appears in column, each number is a jump link to where that term is used in that section (hover to preview the line); the term flashes green when you arrive. Qty counts every mention of the term across the content sections (everything except the summary, this glossary and the references), including repeats within a section. Each term's Topic tag names what it is about, one color per topic.

TermTopicDefinitionAppears inQty
OrchestratorSkillsThe one skill you talk to, client-desk. It sets up clients and calls the module skills; it never touches a channel itself.
Module skillSkillsA small skill for one channel or feature (Messenger, email, meetings, files, launch, sharing) that client-desk calls.
client-deskSkillsThe orchestrator skill, version 1.0.0.
client-messengerSkillsThe live Messenger module, version 2.0.1. Each update makes a new chat page.
Skill cardSkillsThe review card a skill is saved from. Skills are saved only after Swami approves the card.
Skill sheetPagesA page describing one saved skill: what it does, its triggers and its full text.
Build kitDataThe private repo of page builders (client-desk-kit), copied into each client repo at setup.
Client repoDataThe private GitHub repo for one client, holding its data and page sources.
project.jsonDataThe client's main data file: names, status, modules, Drive ids, page links and sharing.
tracker.jsonDataComms log, shared files, tasks and open questions. Modules add rows and never drop them.
channels.jsonDataHolds one "since last" mark per channel.
Since lastUpdatesAn update that covers everything after the channel's last mark, so nothing is missed or repeated.
Update allUpdatesRuns every live module for each active client, then rebuilds the hub and tracker once. Only when asked.
BackfillUpdatesThe first update for a previous client: the whole history, from the first message to now.
Status logLifecycleThe dated list of status changes in project.json, each with a reason.
AdoptLifecycleMoving a client set up before client-desk onto it, in place, without renaming anything.
HubPagesA client's front-door page: status badge, every page, the Drive tree and the repo.
TrackerPagesA client's private page of exchanges, files, tasks and open questions.
Source tagNamingWhere the client came from: FB, Email, Referral, Web, InPerson or Other.
CamelCaseNamingWords joined with no spaces, each starting with a capital, like TestWidget.
Drive for desktopDriveGoogle's app that syncs Drive folders with your computer.
Mirror / Available offlineDriveDrive for desktop settings that keep a folder's files on your computer so they open without a connection.
NDASharingA non-disclosure agreement. NDA material stays private and is checked for before every publish.
FathomUpdatesThe meeting recorder that records and summarises Zoom calls; the planned client-meetings module reads it.
